Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle now. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis are the two openers. Hardik Pandya will start proceedings with the ball. A slip in place too. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Sri Lanka needs to chase the biggest target of this Asia Cup to finish on a high. Their batting has struggled in the Super Four stage, but we cannot deny the quality that they have, and they are also playing with an extra batter that could help them out. However. the Indian attack is one of the best, even without Jasprit Bumrah, and they will be confident of defending this and going into the final as the only undefeated side. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Sri Lanka will be disappointed with their overall bowling effort. While the catching was sharp, the ground fielding let them down as they leaked far too many easy runs. The fifth-bowler issue cropped up once again, despite managing a couple of wickets. The combined four overs from Charith Asalanka and Dasun Shanaka went for 41. Apart from Nuwan Thushara, every other bowler picked up a wicket, but none managed to keep the economy rate under 9, which summed up a tough outing with the ball.

The Powerplay unfolded as expected, with Abhishek Sharma setting the tone through some brilliant ball-striking, while Shubman Gill couldn’t make much of an impact this time. SKY’s lean run carried on, but that hardly bothered the left-hander, who powered to his third consecutive fifty - though once again failing to kick on to a bigger score, something Yuvraj Singh might surely remind him about. Tilak Varma and Sanju Samson then took charge in the middle overs, ensuring the scoring rate stayed around 10 an over. Samson chipped in with a brisk 39, while Tilak held firm with an unbeaten 49. Some lusty blows from Axar Patel at the death carried them past the 200 mark, right off the final ball of the innings.

India have smashed the highest total of this Asia Cup, crossing the 200-run mark for the first time in this edition! It was a powerful batting display, something we’ve consistently seen from the Men in Blue right through the tournament. Blistering starts, attacking play in the middle overs, and this time, after a couple of games where the finish was lacking, they’ve closed things out in style with the bat - a timely boost heading into the final.

SIX! Axar Patel finishes off in style! A full toss outside off. Axar Patel shuffles a long way across off and smashes it flat and over deep mid-wicket for a six. The third umpire, however, checks whether the ball bounced before the ropes. But the replay shows that it has clearly sailed over the boundary. 13 off the final over. INDIA FINISH ON 202/5.

OUT! STRAIGHT UP IN THE AIR, AND GONE! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! This is a screamer of a catch from Dushmantha Chameera! Outstanding effort from the Sri Lanka premier pacer! Hardik Pandya is rushed into the pull shot, but the ball kicks up a bit and takes the top edge. It flies high up, over mid on. Dushmantha Chameera turns around from his follow-through and runs backward, covering a lot of ground. Dives forward with both his hands stretched in front of him and grabs a superb catch. Hardik Pandya departs for 2 (3) and India have slipped a bit from 158/3 to 162/5.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! At the halfway mark, India are exactly 100/3. With the batting depth and power that they have, they will want to double this in the next ten. However, they have two relatively new batters in the crease who will just take a couple of overs before changing gears. Sri Lanka needs to use this phase to get a couple of cheap overs and make the batters try to do something out of the ordinary, which can create opportunities for them. The spinners will have a crucial role to play now and could make or break this game. Also, Wanindu Hasaranga (1-0-4-1) to bowl after the break. He replaces Charith Asalanka.

Abhishek Sharma rocks back and pulls it aerially, but plays closely to his body and hence, does not get the required power and distance to sail it behind deep mid-wicket. The ball descends to the deep mid-wicket fielder, where Kamindu Mendis moves a bit to his right, and takes a well-judged catch, right at the edge of the boundary ropes. Abhishek Sharma misses out on yet another ton, as he departs for a breezy 61 off just 31 deliveries. India are 92/3 down now.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Sweetly timed! Full and into the slot, around off. Abhishek Sharma picks it up and lofts it inside out over cover, beating long off to his right for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.3: Dasun Shanaka to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, onto the pads, nudged across to deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.2: Dasun Shanaka to Tilak Varma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Overthrows! Full from Shanaka, around off. Abhishek shimmies down the track and smashes it straight to mid off. Calls Varma through for a single and the southpaw responds well. Abhishek is running at the danger end and has to hurry as the mid off fielder scores a direct hit at the bowler's end. However, Abhishek has dragged the bat inside in time. The ball deflects off the stumps and rolls to the leg side, allowing the batters to pinch another run. So, two runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.1: Dasun Shanaka to Tilak Varma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Starts off with a loosener. Down leg on a fuller length, Tilak misses to flick. Wide called.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.1: Dasun Shanaka to Tilak Varma, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Double change - Dasun Shanaka replaces Nuwan Thushara. Sri Lanka have struggled with their fifth bowler throughout this Asia Cup, and Shanaka needs to do well here.
Short and outside off. Tilak Varma hangs back and punches it down to the left of long off for a single. An excellent start for Wanindu Hasaranga. Just 4 runs from his first and a big wicket of SKY.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.6: Wanindu Hasaranga to Tilak Varma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tilak Varma comes out to the middle now.

OUT! LBW! Wanindu Hasaranga makes his presence felt in his very first over as he fishes out the Indian skipper. Hasaranga dishes out a flighted delivery, on the middle stump line, on a fullish length. It lands and just spins away a shy bit from the pitch. Suryakumar Yadav premeditates the shot and goes for a sweep, but misses out on it. The ball passes close to the inside edge and hits his front pad. A very confident shout for LBW, and up goes the finger instantly. Suryakumar Yadav walks to chat with Abhishek Sharma and decides to send it upstairs for a review. It looks pretty straight, if there is no edge. UltraEdge shows no bat involved and the Ball Tracking comes up with three reds. The on-field decision is upheld. Suryakumar Yadav departs for 12 (13), and his lean run with the bat continues. India are 74/2.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.5: Wanindu Hasaranga to Suryakumar Yadav, OUT! lbw b Wanindu Hasaranga.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower googly, at just 79.8 kph. Short and outside off. Abhishek Sharma hangs deep and cuts it to deep extra cover for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Wanindu Hasaranga to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pulls the length back, on middle. Suryakumar Yadav is rushed on the back foot and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Wanindu Hasaranga to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: The physio comes in running for a mandatory concussion check. SKY got hit on his helmet, but it was a soft blow and now he is good to go again.

A googly, full and spinning back into the batter from middle. Suryakumar Yadav sits down on his knee and attempts to sweep shot, but he is very early into the shot and misses. The ball pops off the deck and hits his helmet grill.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Wanindu Hasaranga to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dragged length, around off and turning in a bit. Abhishek Sharma rocks back and pulls it uppishly to the left of long on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Wanindu Hasaranga to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A bit of relief for Sri Lanka as the field restrictions have been lifted now. However, they need to stop Abhishek Sharma or else this could get away from them in the blink of an eye. Here comes their most lethal weapon - Wanindu Hasaranga.

Back of a length, around off. Abhishek Sharma stands tall and punches it between mid off and cover for a quick single as the mid off fielder intercepts it with a dive to his right. 12 off the over. 27 from the last two overs. India end their Powerplay strongly with 71/1 on the board.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slams the deck hard on middle. Abhishek Sharma bunts it down the pitch.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! FIFTY FOR ABHISHEK SHARMA! Off just 22 deliveries! His third consecutive half-century! Slower delivery, short into the pitch, on middle and leg. Abhishek Sharma dances down the track, waits for it, and pulls it over wide square leg for a boundary. Another solid knock so far from him. He is looking very dangerous as his rich vein of form continues.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Poor delivery and punished! Full toss, outside off. Abhishek Sharma liberates his arms and smashes it over cover for a boundary! The 50-RUN STAND comes up between the batters now!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Excellent fielding! Abhishek Sharma didn't bother to run quickly as he thought it might run away to the fence. On a good length, on off. Abhishek Sharma shimmies down the track and lofts it over mid on. The ball lands in the long on region, before the ropes and just slows down. Charith Asalanka from the inner circle runs after it and flicks it into the playing area with a sharp dive. Two taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Slingy delivery, too full and on middle. Suryakumar Yadav shapes to flick that to the leg side, but gets a thick leading edge. The ball runs behind square on the off side for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Nuwan Thushara to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Change of ends for Nuwan Thushara. 2-0-21-0 so far, and he replaces Maheesh Theekshana.

FOUR MORE! 15 runs off Dushmantha Chameera's first over! He lands this back of a length and around off, Abhishek Sharma once again makes some room and goes the other side. Slices it towards the third man fence for another boundary. He moves into the 40s now!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Dushmantha Chameera to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Good shot! Bangs in a bouncer, on middle, gets a bit of extra bounce as well. Abhishek Sharma steps across to get inside the line of the ball and hooks it over short fine for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Dushmantha Chameera to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Dushmantha Chameera sees the batter back away, hits the length hard and on middle and off. Abhishek Sharma goes a bit too far away from the ball and slashes but fails to connect.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Dushmantha Chameera to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: NEW BALLS, PLEASE! We are just 4.3 overs into the game, and it seems like the current ball has lost its shape already. And understandably so, as it has taken quite a beating and tour around the park. The fourth umpire comes out with the briefcase of replacement balls. Both the on-field umpires choose one of them and we are good to continue.

SIX! Cracking shot! Fuller in length and around leg, takes pace off too, Abhishek Sharma quickly backs away to make room. He gets under it nicely and dispatches it with ease over the long off fence for a biggie. 50 up for India!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Dushmantha Chameera to Abhishek Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on middle, Suryakumar Yadav clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Dushmantha Chameera to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: So close! Dushmantha Chameera hits the good length on off, jags back in sharply after hitting the deck. SKY tries to play at it from the crease but gets beaten on the inside edge as the ball just zips over the off pole.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Dushmantha Chameera to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Chameera time? Certainly. Here's Dushmantha Chameera into the attack now, replacing Nuwan Thushara.
Goes short and on middle, turns in, Suryakumar Yadav stays back and nudges it through mid-wicket for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Maheesh Theekshana to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Elegant stroke! Pushed through quicker, full and on off again, Suryakumar Yadav this time leans onto his drive nicely and creams it through covers for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Maheesh Theekshana to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up, full and on off, turns in, Suryakumar Yadav looks to drive it away but gets an inside edge onto the pads as the ball goes nowhere.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Maheesh Theekshana to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted, full and around off, Suryakumar Yadav strides out and pushes it throughj covers for a brace.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Maheesh Theekshana to Suryakumar Yadav, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Quicker, full and on middle, Abhishek Sharma tries to heave it across the line but gets an inside edge through backward square leg for a single. Abhishek is looking a bit jittery.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Maheesh Theekshana to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: JUST SHORT! Short and around off, Abhishek Sharma tries to cut it away but hits it uppishly towards point. Charith Asalanka dives forward but the ball just drops in front of him.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Maheesh Theekshana to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Change? Not yet. Maheesh Theekshana is back on the field and is ready to bowl his second over. Went for 14 runs, but took an important wicket of Gill off his first over.
In the blockhole, on leg, Abhishek Sharma tucks it towards mid-wicket for one. 14 runs off the over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Streaky, but they all count! This is pitched up and around middle. Abhishek Sharma backs away and tries to slog it to the leg side a bit too hard. Loses his shape and gets an inside edge that races past short fine for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: NO BALL AND FOUR! Uh, oh! Nuwan Thushara loses his grip and bowls a very high full toss, outside off. Abhishek Sharma is not going to miss out on that and extends his arms to launch it over point for a boundary. It is way above the waist of the batter and a Free Hit will follow now.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, No ball and Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Well bowled! Nails the yorker, on middle, swinging in, Abhishek Sharma just about squeezes it out off the inside half of the bat wide of short fine. The fielder does not put in a dive and lets it roll and the batters come back for the second run. The Lankans have been a bit sloppy in the field!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower one, full and on middle, Suryakumar Yadav knocks it wide of mid on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Nuwan Thushara to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full toss, on middle, Suryakumar Yadav is not expecting that and just drills it towards mid on. Thushara has still not found his rhythm here.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Nuwan Thushara to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and on leg, shapes in, Abhishek Sharma fails to flick it away as the ball goes off his pads towards short fine. The fielder dives to his left but lets it through and the batters gets a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Maheesh Theekshana has walked off the field. The catch he grabbed on 1.3, to dismiss Gill, might have stung him really hard, and he is out to get a bit of treatment. We can see him apply the icepack to his left hand.

Good fielding! Short again and outside off, Abhishek Sharma cuts it wide of point, where the fielder dives to his left and gets a hand to it. That takes the sting out of the ball as the batters cross. Three runs saved.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Maheesh Theekshana to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Up and over! Maheesh Theekshana dags his length back and around off, Abhishek Sharma makes a bit of room and goes hard at it. He ends up slicing it due to the extra bounce over point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Maheesh Theekshana to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Loops it up, full and just outside off, turns away, Abhishek Sharma backs away and offers no shot at it. Called a wide. Harsh call!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Maheesh Theekshana to Abhishek Sharma, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Slows it up, full and on off, Suryakumar Yadav eases it towards long off for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Maheesh Theekshana to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: The Indian captain, Suryakumar Yadav, is in at 3.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! That is a magnificent catch from Maheesh Theekshana! He flights it up, full and around off, sticks to the surface a bit. Shubman Gill goes for the drive but plays it early as the ball flies off the bottom half of the bat towards the bowler. Theekshana, on his follow-through, flings himself to the left side and grabs it with his outstretched hands and more importantly, holds onto it when he lands on the ground. Gill is left stunned but has to walk back for 4 off 3, and India are 15/1!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Maheesh Theekshana to Shubman Gill, OUT! c & b Maheesh Theekshana.

Commentary.Commentary: Misses out! A full toss, on middle, Abhishek Sharma backs away but mistimes his lofted shot towards mid off, where a misfield allows the single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Maheesh Theekshana to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BANG! Welcome to the game, Maheesh Theekshana! He begins with a floater, full and on leg, Abhishek Sharma clears his front leg away and absolutely smokes it over the deep mid-wicket fence for a biggie. Geez, that has traveled miles away into the stands.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Maheesh Theekshana to Abhishek Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Who bowls from the other end? Pace or spin? Spin it will be. Here's Maheesh Theekshana into to the attack.

FOUR! Gets off the mark in style! Nuwan Thushara serves it much fuller this time, on middle, angling into the pads. Shubman Gill steps across and, using his wrists, gently clips it away. He gets good timing on that one as the ball goes over mid-wicket and races to the fence for the first boundary of the game. 8 runs off the first over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Nuwan Thushara to Shubman Gill, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Just pulls his length back a bit around off, shaping away, Shubman Gill reaches out a bit and pushes it to short covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Nuwan Thushara to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good bowling! Nuwan Thushara bowls a good yorker now, on middle, swing in again, Abhishek Sharma gets his bat down in time as the ball goes off the inner half towards deep square leg. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full again and on middle and leg, Abhishek Sharma takes a couple of steps forward and tucks it away, but straight to short mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: First runs off the bat! Pitched up and on the pads, Abhishek Sharma clips it away nicely towards deep square leg. A slight fumble and the batters take advantage of that to get the second run. Good awareness!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! India get underway with extras! Full again but swings a bit too much down the leg side, Abhishek Sharma fails to glance it away. Wided.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Movement right away! Nuwan Thushara starts with a fuller delivery, on middle, shaping in sharply onto the pads, Abhishek Sharma looks to flick it away but misses and gets hit on the pads. A shout for LBW, but turned down. Clearly going down the leg stump!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Nuwan Thushara to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: All the pre-match rituals are done as 'Sri Lanka Matha' and 'Jana Gana Mana' are sung. It is now game time here at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. Not a full house by any means, but still, a buzzing turnout in the stadium, with supporters of both sides turning up in nearly equal numbers. The Lankans spread out of the last-minute huddle and take their respective fielding positions. Shubman Gill walks out with Abhishek Sharma to open for India. Nuwan Thushara has the new ball and is all set to kickoff the proceedings. Off we go...

We are just a few minutes away from the action to get underway. But before that, both sets of players and the match officials are getting lined up for their respective national anthems. It will be Sri Lanka's first, followed by the Indian national anthem.

The live visuals capture the entire Indian squad gathered in the middle, posing together for the commemorative photographs, before the start of the final Super Four clash of this edition of the Asia Cup.

India's TILAK VARMA is up for a quick chat with the broadcasters. He mentions that he tries to finish games off. Highlights that it came at the right moment for him against Pakistan. On his batting position, he shares that he has batted at several positions over the last couple of years, so he is used to it. Shares that Gautam Gambhir, their head coach, has said that everyone should be flexible in the batting order, and says that as a batting unit, they are mentally ready for every position. Tells that he tries to bat according to the game situation. Also says he is stressing more on fitness, saying that he is spending a lot of time in the gym, sharing that he takes a lot of inspiration from Virat Kohli in this regard. On the conditions, Varma mentions that the pitches in Dubai have been a bit on the slower side. Details that he has spoken to SKY about tonight's pitch, and reckons that it looks much better. But also tells it is still slow as compared to the Indian conditions.

PITCH REPORT - Simon Doull and Ravi Shastri are pitchside with their thoughts. Simon first begins by sharing that it is the same pitch that was used in the India vs Bangladesh game. Also highlights that the scores around 160-170 haven't been chased easily. Also adds that there has been some help for the spinners. Ravi joins and says it is a good opportunity for the batters to go out and get big runs. Reckons that the surface will remain good throughout as it has played out nicely so far. Stresses that the bowlers need to give the ball the chance to swing, as the batters will come after them in the first six overs.

The Indian captain, Suryakumar Yadav, says that they would have batted first anyway. Adds that they have been playing good cricket and just wants to stick to their plans. Mentions that dropping catches is a part of the game, but you have to want the ball to come to you to make a difference. Informs that Jasprit Bumrah and Shivam Dube have been rested. Arshdeep Singh and Harshit Rana come in the team.

The captain of Sri Lanka, Charith Asalanka, says they know that they cannot qualify for the final,  but they will treat this as a very important game. Looking at the track, he stresses that they will try to restrict them to 170-175. Mentions that the Lankan openers have been really consistent up top. Informs that they are going with one change for this game, as Janith Liyanage comes in for Chamika Karunaratne.

India (Playing XI) - Abhishek Sharma, Shubman Gill, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Hardik Pandya, Tilak Varma, Axar Patel, Sanju Samson (WK), Kuldeep Yadav, Varun Chakaravarthy, Arshdeep Singh (In place of Jasprit Bumrah), Harshit Rana (In place of Shivam Dube).

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kusal Perera, Charith Asalanka (C), Kamindu Mendis, Janith Liyanage (In place of Chamika Karunaratne), Dasun Shanaka, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dushmantha Chameera, Maheesh Theekshana, Nuwan Thushara.
TOSS - Charith Asalanka calls it right and Sri Lanka have elected to BOWL first.

India, on the other hand, have already sealed their spot in the final where they will meet arch-rivals Pakistan, and remain the only unbeaten team in the tournament. Their success has been built on explosive starts from Abhishek Sharma and Shubman Gill at the top, while Hardik Pandya has stepped up on occasions when the middle order looked shaky. With the ball, Jasprit Bumrah has led the charge as expected, but the real damage has consistently come from Kuldeep Yadav and Varun Chakaravarthy in the middle overs, strangling opposition line-ups. That said, with the final looming, India could use this game to rotate their squad, test their bench strength, and keep their main players fresh for the big showdown. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

Sri Lanka come into this clash as the defending champions from the last time the Asia Cup was played in this format back in 2022. They began their campaign like champions too, winning all three group stage games, but faltered in the Super Fours with back-to-back defeats. The main struggle has been finding the right balance - whenever they’ve gone with an extra bowler, the batting has failed to deliver, and when they’ve opted for an extra batter, they’ve leaked runs. Still, there have been a few positives - Pathum Nissanka’s consistency at the top, Kusal Mendis regaining form, Dasun Shanaka showing his all-round ability, and flashes of brilliance from the pacers. Wanindu Hasaranga, as always, has been their standout performer. But if Sri Lanka are to challenge India here, they will need a complete team effort and big performances across departments.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the final Super Four clash in the Asia Cup 2025. It’s a contest played purely for pride, with no bearing on the qualification race. India have already booked their spot in the final, while Sri Lanka are out of contention. Still, the Lankans will be eager to sign off on a positive note and give their fans something to cheer about before heading home, while India will look to keep their momentum rolling into the title decider.
... MATCH DAY ...

India and Sri Lanka meet in the last match of Super Four in the Asia Cup 2025, but the stakes couldn’t be more different for the two sides. India have already sealed their place in the final and will face either Bangladesh or Pakistan in the summit clash, while Sri Lanka are out of the reckoning and will only be playing for pride. For India, this game is about fine-tuning their combinations and keeping the winning momentum going - Abhishek Sharma’s explosive starts, Shubman Gill’s consistency, and the middle order’s depth including all-round prowess of Hardik Pandya and Shivam Dube have made them look a complete batting unit. Add to that the variety in bowling with Kuldeep Yadav’s guile, Varun Chakaravarthy's mystery, Jasprit Bumrah’s class, and Arshdeep Singh’s death-overs skill, and they look like the team to beat. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, have had a disappointing Super Four campaign where their batting failed to stand up under pressure and the bowling lacked consistency outside of Wanindu Hasaranga’s brilliance. Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis, and Dasun Shanaka will need to lead with the bat, while the bowlers like Nuwan Thushara and Dushmantha Chameera must show more discipline to challenge India. Though the result won’t change the table, Sri Lanka will be desperate to bow out on a high, while India will want nothing less than a dominant display to carry their momentum into the all-important final.
